01 / INSIDE THE AGENT LOOPCONTEXT → ACTION → OBSERVATION → NEXT DECISION

The next step
depends on what comes back.

An Agent is a model inside an execution loop. The request, conversation, available tools, and scoped resources shape its next action. New evidence can change that action—and the plan. The loop is a backend-independent requirement; this exhibit follows the inspected LangGraph route.

MODEL-DRIVEN ADAPTATION

A weak hit changes the query.

The prompt asks the Agent to refine keywords, category, or format when candidates are weak. A structured tool error is another observation; the model may choose a different call or explain the gap.

ADAPTER-LEVEL RECOVERY

A retry is a different mechanism.

The business API adapter can refresh a rejected service token and repeat its call once. ASR/OCR default to at most three attempts with backoff; HTTP 4xx errors stop immediately. These adapter retries do not replan the user’s task.

IMPLEMENTATION / HARDENING

A graph ceiling is not a retry budget.

The inspected configuration sets a 999-step recursion ceiling. Per-task deadlines, model-call budgets, and a common retry policy are additional hardening—not guarantees provided by this exhibit.

The harness supplies capabilities; the model chooses among them. LangGraph is the supported backend used by the inspected application. A custom Rust runtime can provide the same Agent contracts. The inspected construction combines create_deep_agent, registered tools, three storage routes, a general-purpose library subagent, and a custom transcription role. Planning is optional. The parent is instructed to perform ASR first and delegate transcript post-processing only when needed. Purpose summaries here describe visible decisions, not private model reasoning.

SUPPORTED BACKEND IMPLEMENTATION ROUTESONE AGENT CONTRACT · MULTIPLE RUNTIMES

LangGraph is one route.
Rust can carry the same system.

The architecture requires scoped context, adaptive model decisions, tool execution, state, and a user-facing stream. LangGraph supplies one backend route. A custom Rust runtime can implement the same requirements and add precise control for more demanding operational scenarios.

AUTHORIZED CONTEXT→MODEL ⇄ TOOLS + OBSERVATIONS→STATE + USER INTERFACE

The model still chooses the next action. Backend selection chooses how that action is scheduled, stored, recovered, and delivered.

HARDER SCENARIOS / RUST DESIGN PATH

Own the execution policy
when the workload needs it.

A Rust backend can combine the same model-driven Agent loop with bounded asynchronous tool calls, tenant admission budgets, durable continuations, worker fencing, and reconciliation of uncertain external effects. These mechanisms extend the runtime around the Agent’s decisions.

The included Rust kernel demonstrates typed dispatch, snapshot/reducer semantics, version-bound recovery checks, bounded cycles, and an uncertainty ledger. A full backend builds on that foundation with model/tool clients, durable storage, asynchronous workers, and transport. Both routes can support demanding workloads; the guarantees come from those mechanisms and their validation.

Inspect the executable Rust kernel →Download Rust source + tests ↓LangGraph runtime ↗Rust async runtime primitives ↗

Frontend integration: preserving the existing React SDK requires a Rust adapter that implements its thread/run, message/value, cancellation, and error contracts. A custom Rust API uses a corresponding frontend adapter. Backend routes can share the same user experience through either integration.

WORKSPACE CONTRACTOBSERVED IMPLEMENTATION · EXPLAINED AS A MODEL

One workspace.
Three storage contracts.

A draft can look like a file without being an OS file. The runtime routes virtual paths to conversation state, uploaded bytes, or curated knowledge. Each has a different owner, access path, and lifetime.

IMPLEMENTED PATTERN

Follow a file through the boundary.

Examples use synthetic content.

Root-level drafts are graph-state entries. Uploaded files use per-thread disk storage. Curated knowledge is read-only.

WHAT HAPPENS

A composite backend routes paths without requiring the caller to know where the content is stored.

WHY THE BOUNDARY EXISTS

Working context, original evidence, and approved knowledge should not silently overwrite one another.

STORAGE TYPE ≠ RETENTION POLICY

What survives the next event?

{ }STATE-BACKED

Plans, drafts & reports

/plan.md · /final_report.md

Entries inside the graph’s files state. File tools return state updates; they do not create matching files at the host’s root.

SAME THREADThe next step reads the latest state.

Checkpointing can persist this state to disk or a database. “In memory” describes the access model, not a promise that bytes never reach disk.

▤DISK-BACKED

Uploads & derived sidecars

/workspace/input.pdf

Physical files resolved under the selected department and thread directory. OCR, audio, and table tools use these concrete paths.

SAME THREADThe next tool reads the same stored bytes.

The examined implementation defaults workspace TTL to zero: automatic expiry is off. Retained files still need backup, deletion policy, and capacity management.

◇READ-ONLY

Curated knowledge

/knowledge/policy.md

A separate disk mount exposed through a wrapper that rejects writes, edits, and uploads from the agent.

SOURCE CONTROLLEDRead the approved source version.

Read-only is an access rule, not a storage medium. Content updates belong to a separate knowledge-maintenance workflow.

A single virtual file API can sit over three independent stores. It does not make their writes one atomic transaction.

WHAT “THINKING IN MEMORY” MEANS HERE

Explicit reflection and saved drafts are application data: the reflection tool returns a conversation message, while plans and reports update the graph’s file state. These interfaces do not establish that private model-internal reasoning is exposed or durably recorded.

FROM A PERSONAL AGENT TO A SERVICE

The machine is shared.
The authority is not.

A local single-user agent often inherits the operator’s working directory and OS identity. A hosted service has to resolve the caller, department, and thread before selecting a workspace.

01 / IDENTITY

Workspace requests check department access and thread ownership before resolving a physical directory.

02 / EXECUTION

The examined agent does not expose an arbitrary shell. Controlled server adapters invoke tools such as Pandoc and ffmpeg with materialized files.

03 / ISOLATION

A virtual route is an application boundary. OS permissions, process isolation, credentials, and container controls are separate security layers.

CONTAINERS

Package userspace and dependencies. They share a host kernel; CPU architecture still has to match, or use an explicit emulation strategy.

KUBERNETES

IMPLEMENTATION BOUNDARY

Internal news brief selected. Choose an observation or inspect the trace.

WHO CHOOSES?

The model emits tool-call names and arguments. Deep Agents / LangGraph dispatches those calls, adds observations to state, and invokes the model again. A system prompt guides choices; it does not make every branch deterministic.

WHERE DOES IT LIVE?

Root files such as /plan.md and /final_report.md use the graph StateBackend. /workspace/ resolves to a thread’s disk directory. /knowledge/ is a separate read-only disk view.

WHAT IS A RETRY?

A model may revise arguments after a failed result. The business connector separately retries once after its recognized token-authentication response. UI export and voice-input failures return errors to the user; they do not automatically create another agent run.

ACCESS / ROUTING / SCHEDULINGKNOW WHICH BOUNDARY MAKES THE DECISION

Authority before reasoning.
Capacity before dispatch.

A department selects a backend and its resources. The proxy checks access; the model chooses its next action. A production scheduler would make a separate capacity decision.

IMPLEMENTED CONTRACT

Credentials, ownership, then the run.

The registered-department path checks its entry credential and the browser’s ownership of the requested thread. Selecting a department in the UI does not grant access.

Coordination needs

Current boundary: switching departments selects another backend, knowledge root, and browser-scoped history. All department processes load the same orchestrator and tool registry. Inspect the frontend contractVERSIONED EVENTS / IDEMPOTENT REDUCTION +
// One authorized, contiguous public stream per run.
function apply(view, raw) {
  const event = validateV1(raw); // type + payload schema
  if (event.run_id !== view.runId) return view;
  if (event.seq <= view.cursor) return view; // duplicate
  if (event.seq !== view.cursor + 1) return requestResync();
  const next = projectAllowedEvent(view, event);
  return { ...next, cursor: event.seq };
}
The browser owns presentation.
request_id correlates the command; thread_id identifies authorized conversation state; run_id names one execution; seq orders this public stream. Private traces use a separate sequence.
Validate supported schema versions before reduction. Unknown event types trigger an explicit compatibility policy. Render text as text, sanitize approved markup, and allowlist artifact renderers. Never render raw tool HTML.
A new page load restores an authorized snapshot and resumes after its cursor. Native EventSource sends Last-Event-ID on its own reconnect; application-managed reconnects must explicitly carry their saved cursor in a supported request parameter.

REFERENCE 03 / INSIDE THE EXECUTION FRAMEWORKFROM A GRAPH TO A RUNNING SYSTEM

      
The graph is the program.
The runtime makes it run.
A function describes a step. The runtime supplies its environment, reads a consistent snapshot, schedules work, merges updates, and records where execution continues.

      
RUNNABLE RUST · 13 PASSING TESTS
Inspired by LangChain’s composition contracts and LangGraph’s execution model. Re-expressed as a small, inspectable Rust kernel; enterprise distribution and storage remain separate integrations.
Source + tests ↗

      
SEPARATE LIFETIMES. EXPLICIT CONTRACTS.
A graph is executable data.
The program names registered functions and their dependencies. Compiling validates the topology; executing resolves each node to behavior.
CONTRACTGraph(version, nodes, edges) + Registry(NodeId → NodeFn)
LIFETIME
Versioned deployment artifact; shared across invocations.


      
WHAT DOES “PASS A FUNCTION” MEAN?
Behavior is a value.
Authority is an input.
A registry stores a callable: a function pointer or a closure with captured configuration. A task names that callable. At invocation, the runtime lends it state and a scoped context, then receives an update and proposed effects.
An in-memory closure may capture configuration. A checkpoint stores stable node IDs and data, not executable closures, pointers, sockets, or live credentials. A shared long-term store is separate from per-invocation state and must enforce its own access policy.
RUST / CORE CONTRACTSAFE BORROWS · EXPLICIT OUTPUT
type NodeFn = Arc<
    dyn Fn(&State, &RunContext)
        -> Result<Transition, KernelError>
        + Send + Sync
>;

registry.register("finance", Arc::new(finance));
let delta = registry.resolve(node_id)?(
    &snapshot, &scoped_context
)?;

// The scheduler owns progress.
// The reducer owns state composition.
// The gateway owns external effects.
Arc shares ownership; dyn Fn dispatches a callable; borrows carry inputs; Send + Sync express thread-safety obligations. None of these provides a sandbox or persistence. Registration syntax is illustrative; the download is executable.

REFERENCE 04 / THEORY WITH AN OPERATING CONSEQUENCECOMPOSITION · EFFECTS · REDUCERS · CONTROL
The mathematics
has a practical job.
Category theory clarifies valid composition. Computation theory clarifies execution and its limits. Types and tests turn those ideas into contracts a team can review.
THE FORMAL CONTRACT
f : A → B, g : B → C
g ∘ f : A → C
request → normalized query → evidence
PLAINLY
The output of one step must be a valid input to the next. You can assemble reliable behavior from smaller functions.
PRECISELY
For total pure functions, composition is associative and identity preserves behavior. Effectful nodes need a composition law that carries their effects and failure.
Select a concept and inspect its behavior.
The important distinctions: associativity permits regrouping; commutativity permits reordering; idempotence permits duplicate application. These are different properties. Set union has all three. Overwrite is generally order-dependent; floating-point addition is not strictly associative.

REFERENCE 09 / HETEROGENEOUS DEPLOYMENTPORTABILITY IS A LAYERED CONTRACT
Portable services.
Hardware-aware inference.
Domestic CPU, enterprise Linux, and AI accelerators change different compatibility layers. Treat each layer independently.
THE COMPATIBILITY STACK↓
01Application contractsHTTP / gRPC / schemas
02CPU instruction setAArch64 / x86 / other ISA
03User-space ABIglibc or validated musl buildsmusl lives here ↗
04Device runtimeDrivers / firmware / compiler
05Model executionOperators / precision / graphs
A stable libc boundary helps portable services.
It cannot translate instruction sets, replace accelerator drivers, or make every native dependency compatible.
Weights are only
the beginning.
Pin the complete software and device matrix. Audit attention, RoPE, vision encoding, shape handling, and CPU fallbacks before tuning throughput.
  • Match tokenizer, chat template, and visual preprocessing
  • Compare intermediate tensors and task-level quality
  • Profile memory, host-device copies, and tail latency
  • Release by shadow traffic, canary, and reversible versions
RELEASE CRITERION
Equivalent task quality.
Measured device performance.
Verified recovery path.


    
REFERENCE 10 / ENGINEERING JUDGMENTTHE DECISIONS BEHIND THE DIAGRAM
Depth is knowing
what to leave out.
Architecture gets better when each mechanism has a job, an owner, and a reason to exist.
FOUR DECISIONS
WORTH DEFENDING ↘
Agent graphs own reasoning steps. A durable workflow owns business task lifecycle, timers, approvals, and recovery. Two independent engines must not both decide whether the same action should be retried.
Tradeoff / operational machinery is justified by long-running, recoverable work.
Cache entries include identity scope, permission epoch, source version, and processing configuration. Reads still pass authorization. The operation ledger and policy store remain authoritative when the cache is lost or stale.
Tradeoff / more cache fragmentation buys correct isolation and revocation.
Public office, sensitive office, and railway operations have different risk and latency needs. Separate queues, execution pools, and resource budgets reduce blast radius. Shared identity and policy dependencies must still be accounted for.
Tradeoff / reserve capacity and simpler recovery cost more than full utilization.
An agent can collect inputs, explain results, and identify missing evidence. Engineering calculations run in a versioned calculation service with input snapshots, tested formulas, and result receipts. Language fluency is never the numeric ground truth.
Tradeoff / a narrower agent role makes the result auditable and reproducible.
